caseno: Income Tax Reference Application Nos. 521, 522, 523, 524 and 525 of 2007.
lawyer:
MA Hannan with Abdus Samad Azad Advocates ----- For the Applicant in all the Reference Applications. 
Nurun Nahar, AAG ------ For the Respondent in all the Reference Applications.
parties:
City Axis Limited ------- Applicant in all the Reference Applications
Vs
Commissioner of Taxes Dhaka ------- Respondent in all the Reference Applications
full_judgment: "On scrutiny of record it transpires that on wrong interpretation of section 2(8) of IT Ordinance, 1984 the learned AACT has passed his opinion ignoring the actual meaning and sprit of sections 19B/2(8) of the ITO, 1984. As per interpretation of the learned AACT there is no limitation of time in respect of payment of tax u/s 19B. But the legislation does not mean it. As per provision of section 19B, the assessee can avail opportunity under this section if he pays tax before competition of assessment which means this opportunity not remain open when assessment is once completed under any section of IT Ordinance. In section 2(8) of ITO, 1984 every further assessment or re-assessment for the same year i.e u/s 93 or 156 or 159 or 160 whichever is the case may be would be called assessment. But these assessments would not be treated the status of first time assessment. It is very clear that the assessment was completed for the 1st time u/s 83A(1) where the assessee concealed the income and did not submit accurate particulars. Due to concealment of income and submission of inaccurate particulars the cases were re-opened u/s 93 of the ITO, 1984 and assessment were completed u/s 93/84. The assessee paid taxes u/s 19B at his assessee sweet will when the cases were re-open by the DCT for re-assessment. Section 19B allows an assessee a special incentive which must be availed before the making of assessment for the 1st time. So, we think that the order of the Id. AACT in directing to accept investment u/s 19B, was not correct. Hence we vacated the order of the Id. AACT in this respect and restore the original assessment made by the DCT for the assessment years 2000-2001, 2001-2002, 2002-2003, 2003-2004 and 2004-2005."
